content: Overdose with this medication is highly unlikely. However, if someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911 in the United States). If the situation is less urgent, contact a poison control center. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222, and in Canada, you can call 1-844-764-7669. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Levonorgestrel is used by women to prevent pregnancy after birth control failure (e.g., a broken condom) or unprotected sexual intercourse. This medication may be less effective in women over a certain weight (e.g., greater than 164 pounds or 74 kilograms) or if certain other medications have been used within the past month. This reduced effectiveness can result in pregnancy. Always check the ingredients on the label, even if you have used the product before, as the manufacturer may have changed the formulation. Additionally, products with similar names may contain different ingredients intended for different purposes. If you are using an over-the-counter product for self-treatment, carefully read all directions on the product packaging before taking this medication. If you have any questions, consult your pharmacist. Take one tablet orally, with or without food, as soon as possible after unprotected intercourse. After taking this medication, the timing and flow of your menstrual period may change. Notify your doctor immediately if your period is more than seven days late. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, fatigue, dizziness, changes in vaginal bleeding, breast tenderness, or headache. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking levonorgestrel, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other progestins (e.g., norethindrone), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication must not be used during pregnancy. It passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some drugs may reduce the effectiveness of emergency contraception by decreasing the levels of birth control hormones in your body, potentially leading to pregnancy. Examples include griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin), St. John’s wort, drugs used to treat seizures (e.g., barbiturates, carbamazepine, felbamate, phenytoin, primidone, topiramate), and certain HIV drugs (e.g., nelfinavir, nevirapine), among others.
